fix.shows: This is Drèze's follow-up to the column he wrote with Yogendra Yadav in The Indian Express. He sets the rolls of the major states against the Technical Group's projected adults for 2026 and finds them at 99 per cent before the revision and 85 per cent in the draft lists, and the twelve states with final lists at 97, 86 and 88 per cent. He argues that the rolls before the revision already missed many adults, perhaps up to 10 per cent on what he calls patchy evidence, and that dead, shifted and duplicate names hid the gap. Ground reports suggest most deletions of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors were legitimate, he writes. In his account the gap stayed because the second stage demanded documents from electors who were unmapped or had logical discrepancies, when large-scale use of Form 6 could have enrolled the adults who were missing. Assam and Himachal Pradesh are left out of his table.
